correctness.rationale: PASS: For unit rows and consistent equations E||z+||²=||z||²-z^T F(p)z, F=sum p a a^T, so sharp worst-direction decrement equals lambda_min F. The permutation average of any p cannot reduce lambda_min, by concavity; this handles all asymmetrical distributions for global optimality without asserting their uniqueness. With symmetric u,t,v, the leaf-difference eigenvalue is r t (multiplicity m-1) and the orthogonal hub/pooled 2x2 block has trace 1-(m-1)rt and offdiagonal sqrt(m)tcs. Its smaller eigenvalue is at most trace/2 -sqrt(m)tcs, with equality at equal block diagonals. The maximum of the minimum of rising rt and falling affine bound occurs at t=1/Delta; direct substitution of stated u,v equalizes diagonals and attains r/Delta simultaneously in both invariant subspaces. The endpoint c_m arises from the unique physically allowed root of the hub nonnegativity constraint. Independent calculations verified normalization, 2x2 equality and target eigenvalue at m=2,3,5,8 with c=0.3; finite tests do not prove all m. No extrapolation past c_m, where this design becomes infeasible.

value.rationale: PASS: The pooled extra measurement has a distinct algorithmic purpose in redundant projection systems, and its optimal weighting against the hub and leaf directions is a meaningful explicit E-optimal design question. The exact nonzero pooled allocation and sharp phase boundary where the hub measurement becomes unnecessary determine actionable behavior unavailable from a generic SDP restatement. A structural two-block proof covers all m>=2 in the natural feasible range. The result makes no inflated claim to universally optimal Kaczmarz runtime.

final_claim: For each m>=2 and 0<c<=sqrt((3m+2+m sqrt(5))/(2(m^2+3m+1))), the augmented star unit row system a_0=e_0, a_i=c e_0+sqrt(1-c^2)e_i (1<=i<=m), b=m^-1/2 sum_i e_i has optimal fixed-iid worst-direction single-step Kaczmarz mean-square decrement (1-c^2)/[(m+1)(1-c^2)+2sqrt(m)c sqrt(1-c^2)]. A symmetric optimal distribution is the exact hub/leaf/pooled formula in RESULT.md, unique among symmetric distributions; pooled weight is positive for c>0 and hub weight vanishes exactly at the endpoint. No claim is made beyond that parameter range or of nonsymmetric uniqueness.
limitations: The formula is only for 0<c<=c_m, iid fixed probabilities and a consistent system; performance at c>c_m and alternative MSE criteria are outside scope.
The analytic optimizer is unique only among symmetric distributions, not asserted globally unique.
